newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ranariddh snubs offer to return to Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Ranariddh snubs offer to return to Cambodia.

text.p: Deposed Cambodian co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Tuesday spurned an offer by arch rival Hun Sen to guarantee his safety if he returns to Cambodia to face trial.
"I'm not crazy," Ranariddh told reporters at Manila airport before boarding a plane for Bangkok after talks in with Philippine President Fidel Ramos.

Cambodia's new government said on Monday it would guarantee Ranariddh's safety if he returned home but insisted he must face a court to answer charges of weapons smuggling and bringing Khmer Rouge guerrillas into Phnom Penh.
Ranariddh was ousted as co-prime minister last month in a coup staged by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.

The prince has since been touring member countries of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) in search of support in pressuring Hun Sen to hold free elections with royalist forces taking part.

ASEAN - which comprises Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Brunei, Burma and Laos - was to have accepted Cambodia as a new member last month but postponed its entry because of political turmoil in the country.
"Who told you that?" Ranariddh asked after reporters said they had received reports that O'Smach town, the last royalist stronghold in Cambodia, had been taken by Hun Sen's forces.
"I've been in touch this morning, around 8 a.m., with my general in O'Smach and they told me directly from O'Smach that it's okay."
Philippine Lower House Speaker Jose de Venecia, who met Ranariddh on Tuesday, called on the Hun Sen government to drop all charges against the prince as part of a political settlement.

De Venecia proposed the establishment of a new modified coalition government in Phnom Penh "with genuine equal power-sharing in the Cabinet and in the National Assembly to be led by a sole premier, Mr Hun Sen."
Under the formula, Ranariddh would initially serve as special envoy to raise $20 billion from the international community for Cambodia's reconstruction.

After "a reasonable period," Ranariddh and Hun Sen would switch positions, with the prince taking over as solo premier "under a Turkish or Swiss-type model of alternating leadership," de Venecia said.
